title: Weather and why Player left New Orleans after Katrina
summary: Small talk about New Orleans weather, then Player explains he left after Katrina because tourism and musician work collapsed.

blocks.x: Oh, well it’s like maybe 70 degrees, 74 degrees, something like that.
I could tell you’re not quite as comfortable as your wife in this particular area.
Uh no. I need gloves, wader boots, I mean she doesn’t need the scarf.
But you were up here a number of years ago, after Katrina, so there’s some familiar parts to the scene.

Right, right. I came up after Hurricane Katrina and served as the principal for the YMCA Center for the Creative Arts, which was an afterschool program for kids in Rome and Oneida and exposed a lot of kids to jazz music. Yeah it was quite an experience, you know. I came up here after the devastation of Hurricane Katrina in New Orleans, which is where I was living at the time.

Yeah. I mean I think so. You know, after the storm, and even when the city was officially back up and running, there wasn’t much work for musicians at the time, you know, because there weren’t very many tourists coming to the city. And most people know that © Fillius Jazz Archive -1-
